snip.t: Draw three sets of blood cultures from separate venepuncture sites prior to administering antimicrobial therapy.

Model Answer: Obtain three separate sets of blood cultures via distinct peripheral venepunctures, spaced at least 30 to 60 minutes apart, to isolate the causative organism and determine antibiotic sensitivities.

qs.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester develops acute bleeding from multiple venepuncture sites following placental abruption. Laboratory workup reveals prolonged PT and aPTT, severe thrombocytopenia, hypofibrinogenaemia, and a markedly elevated D-dimer. Which underlying pathophysiological process best accounts for this complete laboratory picture?
qs.e: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is characterized by widespread microvascular clotting that consumes platelets and coagulation factors simultaneously, yielding elevated PT/aPTT, low platelets, low fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer. Single factor deficiencies like haemophilia A do not cause consumption of platelets and fibrinogen.

qs.q: A clinical procedure requires rapid intravenous access at the antecubital fossa. Which superficial vein, commonly used for venepuncture, directly connects the cephalic and basilic veins?
qs.e: The median cubital vein connects the cephalic and basilic veins and is routinely utilized for intravenous access and venepuncture. The other vessels listed are deep veins or arteries.
